Train a Model on a Dataset

Source: R/resolve.R
resolve.train.dataset.Rd

Build a model for a dataset loaded with resolve.dataset.csv(), hold out a fold of its plots for early stopping, and train.

Usage

resolve.train.dataset(
  dataset,
  hiddenDims = NULL,
  maxEpochs = NULL,
  patience = NULL,
  fixedEpochs = NULL,
  selectionMetric = NULL,
  lr = NULL,
  lrScheduler = NULL,
  lrStepSize = NULL,
  lrGamma = NULL,
  lrMin = NULL,
  lrPlateauFactor = NULL,
  lrPlateauPatience = NULL,
  lrPlateauThreshold = NULL,
  lrPlateauCooldown = NULL,
  warmupSteps = NULL,
  warmupEpochs = NULL,
  batchSize = NULL,
  device = NULL,
  testSize = 0.2,
  stoppingPlots = NULL,
  seed = 42L,
  savePath = NULL,
  checkpointDir = NULL,
  checkpointEvery = NULL,
  resumeFrom = NULL,
  lossConfig = NULL,
  ncaTemperature = NULL,
  ncaNeighbors = NULL,
  ncaWeight = NULL,
  moeRouting = NULL,
  moePlacement = NULL,
  nExperts = NULL,
  expertHiddenDims = NULL,
  moeTopK = NULL,
  moeNoiseStd = NULL,
  moeAuxLossWeight = NULL,
  coverDropout = NULL,
  plotTotals = NULL,
  plotTotalsDropout = NULL,
  freezeComposition = NULL,
  freezeEncoder = NULL,
  dModel = NULL,
  nHeads = NULL,
  nAttentionLayers = NULL,
  transformerFfDim = NULL,
  transformerPooling = NULL,
  transformerDropout = NULL,
  modelConfig = list(),
  trainConfig = list(),
  pretrain = NULL,
  initFrom = NULL,
  initReuse = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

dataset

A ResolveDataset object from resolve.dataset.csv()

hiddenDims

Hidden layer widths of the encoder MLP.

maxEpochs

Maximum training epochs.

patience

Early stopping patience in epochs.

fixedEpochs

Train exactly this many epochs of the maxEpochs schedule, with no early stopping, and keep the final weights (0, the default, is early stopping). The learning-rate schedule is still laid out over maxEpochs. The only mode that accepts testSize = 0, for a refit on every plot.

selectionMetric

The held-out value early stopping, best_epoch (the returned weights) and a "plateau" schedule follow: "loss" (the default, the lowest selection loss wins) or "accuracy" (the highest held-out accuracy of the dataset's one classification target wins, and a plateau follows PyTorch's ReduceLROnPlateau in mode "max"). "accuracy" needs a held-out fold and exactly one classification target.

lr

Learning rate.

lrScheduler

Learning-rate schedule: "none" (constant), "step" multiplies the rate by lrGamma every lrStepSize epochs, "cosine" anneals it from lr to lrMin over maxEpochs, "linear" lowers it linearly at every optimizer step, from lr at the end of the warmup to lrMin at the last step of maxEpochs, and "plateau" multiplies it by lrPlateauFactor when the held-out value that drives early stopping has not improved for more than lrPlateauPatience epochs (PyTorch's ReduceLROnPlateau, in mode "min" on the loss and "max" on the accuracy, see selectionMetric). "plateau" needs a held-out fold, so it is refused with testSize = 0.

lrStepSize

Epochs between decays under lrScheduler = "step".

lrGamma

Factor of each decay under lrScheduler = "step".

lrMin

The rate the cosine and linear schedules end at, and the floor a plateau never decays below.

lrPlateauFactor

Factor a plateau multiplies the rate by, in (0, 1).

lrPlateauPatience

Epochs without improvement of the held-out value (selectionMetric) a plateau allows; the next one decays the rate. Like patience, an epoch counts only once the loss objective has reached its final phase.

lrPlateauThreshold

Relative improvement on the best held-out value an epoch must make to count as one, in [0, 1) (the default 0 is any improvement, the rule early stopping and best_epoch use; PyTorch's default is 1e-4).

lrPlateauCooldown

Epochs after a decay during which no epoch counts against the rate.

warmupSteps

Optimizer steps over which the rate climbs linearly, from lr / warmupSteps at the first step to the schedule's rate (0, the default, is no warmup). The schedule carries on unchanged after it. An epoch that begins inside the warmup counts against neither patience nor a "plateau" schedule; its held-out value can still be the best.

warmupEpochs

The warmup in epochs instead of steps (each epoch the ceiling(nTrain / batchSize) steps it takes). Give warmupSteps or warmupEpochs, not both.

batchSize

Batch size.

device

Device to train on: "cpu", "cuda" (the current CUDA device) or "cuda:N".

testSize

Fraction of the data held out for early stopping (default 0.2), drawn at random with seed. 0 holds nothing out and needs fixedEpochs.

stoppingPlots

Plot IDs to hold out for early stopping instead of a random testSize fraction (default NULL): a withheld spatial block or database, or the fold a published protocol selects its epoch on. Early stopping, best_epoch, final_metrics and the baselines read exactly these plots; every other plot trains. Each ID must be a plot of dataset, listed once, and at least one plot must be left to train. With a masked target, the fold needs at least one plot labelled for it. Not combined with testSize.

seed

Random seed of the split and the epoch shuffle (default 42).

savePath

Path to save model checkpoint (optional)

checkpointDir

Directory the run writes checkpoints to while it trains (optional): best.pt at every new best epoch, checkpoint_<N>.pt every checkpointEvery epochs, progress.json after every epoch (see resolve.progress()) and checkpoint.pt at the end. best.pt and checkpoint_<N>.pt carry the run's progress, so resumeFrom can continue from them.

checkpointEvery

Also write checkpoint_<N>.pt every this many epochs (0, the default, writes best.pt only). Needs checkpointDir.

resumeFrom

A best.pt or checkpoint_<N>.pt an interrupted run wrote (optional). The run continues at the epoch after it, with its optimizer, early-stopping and random-number state, as if it had never stopped; result$resumed_from_epoch names that epoch. Pass the interrupted run's dataset, model and training arguments and seed, so the split and recipe are the ones it trained on.

lossConfig

Loss configuration: "mae", "smape", "combined" (the default: MAE, then MAE and SMAPE, then the band penalty, by phase), or "nca", which takes the "combined" regression schedule and adds the Neighbourhood Components Analysis term to classification targets.

ncaTemperature

Scale of the stochastic-neighbour softmax in the NCA term, i.e. the effective number of neighbours each sample spreads over. Acts only when lossConfig = "nca".

ncaNeighbors

Neighbours per sample the NCA term sums over, its most similar in-batch samples. Zero or less keeps the whole batch. Acts only when lossConfig = "nca".

ncaWeight

Weight of the NCA term against the cross-entropy it is added to. Acts only when lossConfig = "nca".

moeRouting

Mixture-of-experts routing: "none" (a single dense encoder), "soft" (every expert contributes, weighted by the gate) or "topk" (only the moeTopK highest-gated experts run per plot).

moePlacement

Where the mixture sits: "tail" makes it the encoder's final stage, so hiddenDims minus its last two widths becomes the backbone and the experts produce the latent; "post" runs it over the finished latent instead, preserving the width. "post" is the only placement open to an encoder with no MLP tail. Acts only when moeRouting is not "none".

nExperts

Expert networks in the mixture (at least 2).

expertHiddenDims

Hidden widths inside each expert.

moeTopK

Experts activated per plot under "topk" routing.

moeNoiseStd

Standard deviation of the noise added to the gate logits during training, which spreads load across experts.

moeAuxLossWeight

Weight on the mixture's load-balancing loss, added to the task loss.

coverDropout

Cover-dropout rate applied to species cover values in rank-pool / transformer encoding modes.

plotTotals

Add each plot's combined cover and species count to the rank-pool / transformer features, with a flag saying they are present.

plotTotalsDropout

With plotTotals, the probability that a training plot's totals are withheld, so the model also predicts plots given without them (resolve.plot_totals).

freezeComposition

Keep the species, genus and family embedding tables at their initialisation instead of learning them.

freezeEncoder

Keep every parameter outside the task heads at its value, and run that part in evaluation mode while the heads train. With initFrom, the heads learn on the encoder of the trained parent.

dModel

Model dimension for the transformer / rank-pool encoder.

nHeads

Number of attention heads in the transformer encoder. Ignored unless nAttentionLayers > 0.

nAttentionLayers

Number of self-attention layers in the transformer encoder (0 pools the token embeddings without attention).

transformerFfDim

Feed-forward hidden dimension inside each transformer block.

transformerPooling

Pooling strategy used to collapse the per- species token sequence into a plot embedding: "attention" or "cls".

transformerDropout

Dropout rate applied inside transformer blocks.

modelConfig

Named list of any further ModelConfig fields, for example list(encoder_architecture = "ft_transformer", dropout = 0.1) or list(encoder_architecture = "heterogeneous_gnn", heterogeneous_gnn = list(k_cooccurrence = 10)) (the species graph is built from the dataset).

trainConfig

Named list of any further TrainConfig fields, for example list(weight_decay = 1e-4, use_amp = TRUE).

pretrain

Self-supervised pretraining of the encoder on the dataset's plots before training (optional): a list with method, "jepa", "scarf" or "masked_species" (a transformer-encoded model), and any of that method's settings (resolve.default_config() "pretrain", or "masked_species"), e.g. list(method = "scarf", pretrain_epochs = 20).

initFrom

Fine-tune: start from a trained model, a parent from resolve.parent() or the path of a checkpoint. dataset must be loaded with the parent's vocabs() and dataset_config(); the model takes the parent's configuration, and only the head settings (head_hidden_dims, head_activation, head_dropout), the dropout rates and the freeze settings may differ. The encoder starts from the parent's weights, the coordinates and covariates are scaled as the parent scaled them, and the checkpoint records the parent (resolve.load_run_metadata() parent). Not combined with pretrain.

initReuse

With initFrom: what is carried over besides the encoder, "encoder" (the default: every head starts fresh) or "encoder_heads" (also the head of each target the parent shares under the same name, task, transform and classes, with its scaling).

verbose

Print training progress (default TRUE)

Value

A list with trainer, result, dataset and, with pretrain, pretrain (the pretraining's loss_history, total_time_seconds and epochs_completed). result carries best_epoch, train_time_seconds, final_metrics, the loss histories train_loss and test_loss (one value per epoch), the learning rate each epoch trained at lr (the rate of its last optimizer step, which warmup and "linear" move within an epoch), the held-out value of selectionMetric each epoch scored selection (the held-out loss, or the accuracy; empty when nothing is held out), the loss histories' split by target train_loss_by_target and test_loss_by_target (named lists of per-epoch vectors: each target's weighted term of the total, so per epoch they add up to it), train_aux_loss (a named list of the auxiliary terms of train_loss, which belong to no target, each already weighted: moe, the mixture-of-experts load balancing, and tabnet_sparsity, TabNet's feature-mask sparsity; empty for a model with neither), the per-target baselines (the model against the training mean or mode, regression values in original units), diagnostics, effective_batch_size – the batch size the run actually trained at, which is smaller than batchSize when the CUDA auto-halve-on-OOM retry fired – and resumed_from_epoch (0 unless resumeFrom continued the run).

Details

Every model and training setting has the RESOLVE engine's default (resolve.default_config() "model" / "train"). The named arguments below set the common ones; modelConfig and trainConfig reach every field of the RESOLVE engine's ModelConfig and TrainConfig, nested architecture configs included (encoder_architecture, ft_transformer, tabnet, saint, gnn, trait_net, excelformer, heterogeneous_gnn, tabm, parallel_layers, and the activation, normalization and head settings). A key the RESOLVE engine does not know is an error, and so is a field set both by a named argument and in the list. The fields that size a model to its data (the species encoding, hash width, top_k and the taxonomy slots) come from the dataset.

Examples

plots <- system.file("extdata", "plots.csv", package = "resolveR")
species <- system.file("extdata", "species.csv", package = "resolveR")
roles <- list(plot_id = "plot_id", species_id = "species", abundance = "cover",
              genus = "genus", family = "family", latitude = "lat", longitude = "lon")
targets <- list(elevation = list(column = "elevation", task = "regression"),
                habitat = list(column = "habitat", task = "classification"))
dataset <- resolve.dataset.csv(plots, species, roles = roles, targets = targets)
fit <- resolve.train.dataset(dataset, maxEpochs = 20L, verbose = FALSE)
fit$result$final_metrics$elevation$r2

ft <- resolve.train.dataset(dataset, maxEpochs = 5L, verbose = FALSE,
                            modelConfig = list(encoder_architecture = "ft_transformer"))
